Maya Patel: Quick async standup — API GW / routing / auth / rate limits
Maya Patel: yesters: finished the canary policy shim and added fallback routing for model inference lanes. validated on staging (small traffic).
Maya Patel: blockers: still seeing occasional 429s in staging when prefix cache misses spike, trying to reproduce with load generator.
Maya Patel: today: pair with @Jordan on the token-bucket tweak, and open CR for the config migration script.

Jordan Lee: nice. can you drop the staging logs here for the 429s? any pattern on seq lengths?

Maya Patel: logs: pasted snippet below — looks like bursts from thin-client tests, seq len ~64-128.
Maya Patel: ```
[2024-06-01T15:12:03Z] gw-proxy: 429 throttle exceeded route=/v1/generate model=redwood-large seq=128 tokens=64 tenant=acme-corp
[2024-06-01T15:12:03Z] gw-proxy: backlog=120 batch_size=8 inflight=3
```

Ravi Singh: @Maya could be batching fallback kicking in. We saw similar with the old prefix cache evictions. Did you enable the new KV cache retention flag?

Maya Patel: yes KV retention = 30m in staging. I think it's a combination: thin-client warmup + canary weight shift.

Sam Torres: CR ping — @Maya opened the migration script PR? I'm on call later, can review after 6pm PT.

Maya Patel: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/489 — small python step to rewrite route policies to new schema. Tests added. requesting review from @Sam and @Lena.

Lena Kim: I'll take a look this morning. one thought: make sure the new schema preserves the legacy rate-limit calc (token vs req).

Maya Patel: good call — added unit that asserts old->new equivalence for a few sample policy matrices.

Jordan Lee: for the token-bucket tweak: let's try reducing burst_fill_ms from 1000 -> 600 for the thin-client lane and watch 95th p50. I can deploy a patch to canary.

Ravi Singh: also may be worth a short-term rule: when queue_length > 100 do aggressive route spillover to dedicated-pool. config snippet:
Ravi Singh: ```yaml
- name: spillover-on-surge
  condition: queue_length > 100
  action: route_to: dedicated-pool
  note: quick fallback to avoid 429 storm
```

Sam Torres: ops question: any risk to SLA if we route to dedicated-pool? cost spike but keeps latency.

Jordan Lee: SLA-wise it's fine for canary; for prod we'd need approval. for staging/canary it's safe.

Maya Patel: timeline: I'll run the reduced-burst canary at 11:30 PT, monitor for 30m. if stable i'll merge the migration PR and schedule the config rollout for next Tue.

Lena Kim: FYI — I added a small eval prompt set to detect quality regressions when switching quantized runtime in dedicated pools. If routing moves traffic to dedicated quantized variant, we'll flag.

Maya Patel: perfect. once CR is green i'll tag @Sam for final review. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [info] canary deployment created: canary-20240601-1730, id=cny-8713. See dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/canaries/cny-8713

Sam Torres: noted — i'll review PR after oncall handoff. if anything urgent ping me in #eng-oncall.

Jordan Lee: quick ask — can someone run a short loadgen against staging with thin-client profile? I can schedule a 20m run at 12:00 PT.

Ravi Singh: I can kick that off. will post results summary here.

Maya Patel: thanks Ravi. last note: tracked task in GH project: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/projects/7#card-1024 — moving to "in progress".
